events.title: Supervisor feedback challenges initial beach robot proposal value proposition
events.result: The first proposal drew critical feedback on value proposition compared with an existing university beach robot, prompting a rethink.

events.title: Revised proposal pivots to reduced-scope manually operated sieve device
events.result: A second proposal with reduced scope was prepared, circulated and sent, with a reply received by the next morning.

events.title: Pain-point review of existing beach robots and edge computing options
events.result: The team listed pain points and candidate solutions, including onboard autonomy and computer vision for open environments.

events.title: Alternative acoustic predictive maintenance proposal submitted to supervisors
events.result: A short pivot proposal was sent but not pursued after being judged too electrical-engineering focused.

events.title: Computer vision navigation direction emailed; supervisors suggest robot-agnostic cleaning add-on
events.result: The email exchange moved the project toward a beach-cleaning add-on that could pair with different autonomous robots.

events.title: In-person supervisor consultation sets direction on an end effector
events.result: The advice was to scope down to an end effector for a defined waste type and demonstrate it on an existing platform.

events.title: Project approved for the robotics studio
events.result: The project was approved, with five groups in the studio.

events.title: Team expands to five with Gary and Yizhang joining
events.result: New members were notified to the studio, joined the opening session period and gained access to a shared project folder.

events.title: Problem scoping work split into five research areas
events.result: Members took computer vision, wear, coastal locomotion, collection systems and modular robotics.

events.title: Problem scoping consultation with course lecturer at E2A
events.result: Feedback asked the team to define its terms, justify claims with numbers and clarify stakeholders.

events.title: Five problem statements agreed and assigned across team
events.result: Three technical and two general problem areas were allocated for Assignment 1.

events.title: Request sent to supervisor for a cleaning-industry contact
events.result: A contact request was emailed, but no resulting interview is shown at that stage.

events.title: Studio session reviews Assignment 1 and books further consultation
events.result: The team met during studio, used a shared board and booked a lecturer review of its documents.

events.title: Lecturer consultation on Assignment 1 documents at E2A
Individual Assignment 1 problem insight reports submitted
events.result: Members reported submitting around the deadline, with later rework possible.

events.title: Peer critique lecture and Assignment 1 rework period
events.result: Students exchanged written critiques, and resubmission based on peer feedback was opened until 16 February.

events.title: Group problem statement drafted around beach worker occupational health
events.result: The draft framed the proof of concept around heat stress and musculoskeletal risks in manual beach cleaning.

events.title: Test bed item obtained for later prototype testing
events.result: A test bed item was requested and obtained, but the chat text gives no description or test.

events.title: Optional morphological matrix tutorial attended
Team working session produces design brief and matrix drafts
events.result: The session produced draft brief and matrix files, early AI-assisted concept images and next steps.

events.title: Draft design matrix submitted for lecturer's class contribution review
events.result: The available matrix was submitted early, while the fuller shared document stayed in progress.

events.title: Post-midterm plan names conveyor-rake and rotating drum-screw prototype directions
events.result: The plan assigned CAD, stakeholder and report tasks, and tied the value case to a modular unit for compact platforms.

events.title: Tracked base for carrier robot partly assembled
events.result: A tracked pulling base was assembled in one afternoon, while the full prototype remained unfinished.

events.title: Outreach emails sent to beach-cleaning operators
events.result: Prepared operator contacts were emailed, and one operator replied the next day.

events.title: Morphological chart redone by hand after studio feedback
events.result: After clarification that the charts differ, four function rows were hand-drawn and added to the shared document.

events.title: Contact made with coastal cleanup community for test opportunities
events.result: A community contact was reported as a possible additional route for testing.

events.title: Interface options reviewed and design requirements pruned
events.result: A universal mounting bracket became the proof-of-concept approach, and the brief and matrix were reported finalised.

events.title: Lecturer gives positive response to the Assignment 2 direction
events.result: The lecturer supported the direction and suggested one concept could show the team's actual intended prototype.

events.title: Studio session sets partner requirements with supervisors
events.result: The team agreed to request an operations interview and prototype test access, with no formal partnership needed.

events.title: Sand quantity prepared for indoor test bed
events.result: The amount of sand was judged enough to show the mechanism at interim but not enough for final testing.

events.title: Assignment 2 submitted and later resubmitted with labelled diagrams
events.result: Members submitted early, and some reworked or resubmitted before the final lecture session.

events.title: Site visit requested from developer of an existing beach robot
events.result: Wonje was asked to follow up after the developer's exams.

events.title: Prototyping lecture and post-class lecturer discussion on interim direction
events.result: Interim requirements and a template were outlined, and team A2 work was shown in class.

events.title: Prototype approach planned using cardboard models and printed top choices
events.result: The plan was five low-fidelity cardboard models and two 3D-printed top choices for mounting trials, time permitting.

events.title: Main prototype direction debated between conveyor and horizontal screw
events.result: The conveyor became the preliminary main prototype for a minimum working build, with the screw and other concepts kept for testing.

events.title: Prototype litter size and conveyor width constraints discussed
events.result: The prototype would target smaller litter of about 15 cm for now, with a conveyor near 30 cm wide and later scale-up.

events.title: Optional tutorial on interim presentation and assessment attended
events.result: The tutorial covered presenting and Q&A, and stricter assessment rubrics were said to be coming.

events.title: Low-fidelity gripper-concept parts modelled and 3D printing begun
events.result: A screw-jointed part was shown and the rest were queued for overnight printing; the link to the gripper concept is inferred.

events.title: Paper Archimedes screw model built inside plastic bottle
events.result: A paper screw inside a bottle was attempted, but a rotating moving demonstration could not be completed in time.

events.title: Studio session sets interim contents, timeline and team responsibilities
events.result: Guidance covered report content, including comparison of solutions, testbedding results and planning charts, and a week-by-week plan was issued.

events.title: Existing beach robot developer responds about viewing and available videos
events.result: The robot was being upgraded, so a working demonstration was unavailable, though videos could be shared.

events.title: First team visit to beach area to photograph litter
events.result: Informal observation suggested large items and small pieces around 5 cm or less were common, with no measurements taken.

events.title: Cardboard rake-conveyor prototype built and tried on a bench
events.result: In an informal trial, the scoop pushed trash forward instead of lifting it, while the belt could carry trash once loaded.

events.title: Rotating drum low-fidelity model moved away from cardboard construction
events.result: A wire-mesh drum with a rigid end base was being designed, and no finished drum is shown at that stage.

events.title: Public technical write-up of an existing beach robot reviewed
events.result: The review captured published drive, phase and sand-ingress details, while an interview was still wanted for maintenance insights.

events.title: Team compared screw, brush-roller and conveyor collection concepts
events.result: Team doubted the screw concept and considered a brush-roller alternative; on 2 Apr the direction settled on conveyor plus gripper.

events.title: Early arm prototype reported working, gripper adaptation proposed
events.result: Arm was reported as basically working but inefficient, with a gripper proposed for larger debris.

events.title: Discrete-element sand simulation of screw concept attempted
events.result: Simulation setup loaded geometry and particles while compatibility errors were being fixed; no simulation result was reported.

events.title: Terrain data logging interface for IMU and odometry prepared
events.result: Logging interface was run in simulation only at first because the test robot battery was low; calibration was due before departure.

events.title: Industry partner site visit at Sentosa beach
events.result: Team observed current beach cleaning operations with an operations interview and recorded workflow and pain points.

events.title: Small robot terrain slip and roughness logging around Sentosa visit
events.result: Two terrain logs dated 2 Apr (11:44 and 15:15) were shared; the slip equation was later questioned by a teammate.

events.title: Evening visit to the SUTD beach robot team
events.result: Team met the SUTD robot team, viewed demonstration footage and later summarised design lessons such as modularity and easy maintenance.

events.title: First concept defined: raked conveyor, mesh-bottom bin, damped mount
events.result: Concept was written down as a conveyor with rakes, a mesh-bottomed bin and a modular mount for a general purpose platform; nothing built to this definition was shown yet.

events.title: Partner and SUTD visit notes summarised and human-verified
events.result: An automated summary of both visits was checked and restructured by hand before use in the problem definition.

events.title: Vibrating whole-bin approach chosen for separation proof of concept
events.result: Team chose to shake the whole bin for the proof of concept, optimising later; isolation mounts were still being discussed on 5 Apr.

events.title: Draft interim slide deck shared with the course instructor
events.result: Instructor response was reported as acceptable for now.

events.title: Interim slides built across team working sessions
events.result: Slides were reworked after review, with section ownership reassigned just before the presentation.

events.title: Causal loop diagram of the beach cleaning system developed
events.result: Diagram captured labour and machine deployment loops and was used in the problem framing.

events.title: Supervisor review of draft interim slides
events.result: Feedback asked for more specific, bounded requirements, a clearer link to stakeholders, and technical grounding on motors and power budget.

events.title: Conveyor sizing model and technical specification drafted
events.result: A scripted sizing model and specification were drafted, with final values dependent on later empirical tests and outputs not yet verified.

events.title: Mounting concept with extrusions, base plate and locking brackets designed
events.result: Vibration loosening was raised in review, and an extra bracket and locking fasteners were added; load figures were calculated from assumptions, not measured.

events.title: Subsystem test plan and success criteria drafted
events.result: Draft plan was written, including proposed frame deflection and clamp force retention checks; none of those tests are shown as run.

events.title: Gripper arm built and bench-tested picking up small debris
events.result: Some takes succeeded and others did not on flat ground; the base servo was unavailable, so the base was excluded and picks were limited to items directly in front.

events.title: Reduced-scale conveyor prototype bench-tested on dry sand
events.result: Report text states the conveyor was bench-tested on dry sand with first-iteration cleats; mass, power draw and sand collected per rake were not measured, and exact test dates are inferred.

events.title: Cam clamp mount part 3D printed
events.result: Printing was reported under way; completion was not explicitly stated.

events.title: Bin size reduced and vibration cradle alternative proposed
events.result: The earlier bin size was judged too tall, a roughly 25 L bin was proposed, and a cradle or mesh cage was added as an alternative in the selection matrix.

events.title: Rotating drum prototype tested as a separation alternative
events.result: Team notes list the drum test as done by 15 Apr and the team chose to focus on the drum, with no measured figures; dates are approximate and a report excerpt says the full separation subsystem was not yet fabricated.

events.title: Interim presentation to examiners with prototypes
events.result: Team presented on Friday morning in the week 12 slot, with prototype photos added during the session; examiners pushed further alternatives, including centrifugal separation of sand.

events.title: Four-class debris classification defined for the design scope
events.result: The team defined its own classification and targeted classes 1 to 3, leaving the largest objects to manual handling.

events.title: Concept and plans shared with industry partner for feedback
events.result: The partner's operations contact gave a brief positive response based on a shared screenshot, without a detailed review.

events.title: Post-interim team meeting turned feedback into report actions
events.result: Actions covered current operations, debris classes, modular payload, wet sand, success criteria and a revised project plan.

events.title: Prototype tests with sand shaking and branch debris
events.result: Tests were arranged for that day and clips were posted that afternoon, but the chat does not describe the video contents or outcome.

events.title: Technical specifications based on a commercial outdoor robot's dimensions
events.result: The team chose to size the design against published Husky platform dimensions without obtaining that platform.

events.title: Seaweed debris test on the prototype
events.result: A test clip was shared; the chat does not state the outcome or name the mechanism, which is inferred as the conveyor.

events.title: Initial contact made with a marine cleanup group
events.result: An introduction was reported, with possible relevance to project outreach; no follow-up is shown.

events.title: Motor references finalised for conveyor and drum power estimates
events.result: Task was marked complete; the chat gives no measured power figures.

events.title: Concept of operations rewritten with partner workflow and site notes
events.result: The robot was described as remotely supervised with automatic debris collection on wet lower-beach zones, and site notes were added to the appendix.

events.title: Design direction summarised: conveyor, untangling spokes, rotating drum, bin
events.result: Summary was agreed in chat, with chain-style quick links and road-transit handling of the conveyor noted as open items.

events.title: Team reviews robot base options after the small platform proves unsuitable
events.result: Options discussed included the lab rover, a retrofit, a manual trolley for testing and a modified ride-on toy base; no choice was made and it was deferred to the summer. The existing platform was recalled as having stalled on sand about a minute in with no load (earlier test, date not given here).

events.title: Survey of commercial robot chassis as platform options
events.result: Tracked and wheeled chassis were compared; bought bases looked impractical for the project, and ride-on toy bases were doubted for torque and lack of a comms interface.

events.title: Lab rover identified as Copernicus and its public documentation located
events.result: The ROS wiki page, a video and the source repository were found, and the rover was viewed as the best base available to the team.

events.title: Attempt to relocate the Copernicus rover to the team workspace
events.result: Moving the rover was not approved, so work stayed in Studio 3; a second robot was identified as another possibility.

events.title: Copernicus rover opened and internal electronics inspected in Studio 3
events.result: The rover was disassembled and documented before any functional test; the team found the available code covers only the ROS driver, while the motor-driver link through the onboard STM32 firmware is proprietary. Replacing the board with a power board and a Raspberry Pi was proposed as an option.

events.title: Prior student report reviewed and motor-driver RS485 register map obtained
events.result: The earlier report recorded the rover computer losing contact with its controller near the end of that semester; the driver vendor supplied the register map, and the team planned to rewire and test ROS first, with a simple power circuit as fallback. The rover vendor had not responded.

events.title: Copernicus reassembly and ROS bring-up attempt without motion
events.result: The rover did not move while the STM32-to-FTDI link was being checked, and the onboard computer then stopped powering on. The team decided to bypass the original board and drive the motors through a USB-RS485 adapter from a Raspberry Pi.

events.title: Second robot base opened and assessed for use
events.result: Internals were photographed and were tidy and labelled, but with no documentation and an unsuccessful charging attempt the base was judged not usable.

events.title: Copernicus motors driven directly over USB-RS485, bypassing the original controller
events.result: Motors responded to direct commands, and a wrongly set termination resistor on the first driver was found to be blocking the second. The onboard computer was confirmed dead, the STM32 fault stayed undiagnosed, the baud rate was raised from 19200 to address latency, and a control guide was written.

events.title: Informal evening observation of debris at East Coast beach
events.result: A team member saw and filmed debris on the beach during a casual visit; no measurements were taken.

events.title: Copernicus STEP model reverse engineered from mesh files
events.result: A STEP file derived from the vendor mesh was shared, and the rover's dimensioned drawings and user manual were circulated.

events.title: Trommel drum concept adopted for sand separation in place of vibrating bin
events.result: The team settled on a conveyor feeding a sloped rotating mesh drum, with a plastic prototype first and metal later; seaweed handling was left as an open question to test, and early sizes were later revised.

events.title: Benchmarking of existing beach-cleaning machines and mechanisms
events.result: Belt-based machines were reviewed online, with doubts raised about whether that type could pick up seaweed.

events.title: Copernicus teleoperated drive test using Raspberry Pi and RS485 link
events.result: The rover ran on video and was considered acceptable, but the left wheels lagged the right, which the team attributed to the daisy-chained bus; teleoperation was later reported as wired.

events.title: Conveyor, drum and bin layout and sizes agreed for the build
events.result: The plan was a 430 mm spoked conveyor, a conversion plate into a 430 mm diameter motorised drum, an inverted V plate shedding sand off the sides, and a 430x360x430 mm bin hanging off the top panel; drum length and packaging remained open.

events.title: Copernicus main board schematic redrawn and its bypassed state reviewed
events.result: A schematic was produced; the team recorded that switches and the motor relay were shorted because the relay did not trigger, some regulators did not work and the outputs sat at battery voltage. A new PCB was set aside in favour of disconnecting the battery when idle.

events.title: Copernicus body and payload rail dimensions measured
events.result: Measured 460 mm wide by 650 mm long, with rails 509 mm long, 416 mm across, 40 mm individual width and a 10 mm slot.

events.title: Supervisor check-in on capstone progress during summer internships
events.result: The team reported the rover repair and teleoperation but little capstone build progress, and set a target of a preliminary design and parts list by week 0.

events.title: Supervisor feedback on fit with the existing site cleaning workflow
events.result: The supervisor asked about retrofitting existing tractors and how the robot fits the current workflow, prompting the team to state this more clearly.

events.title: Copernicus CAD baseline built in a shared Fusion workspace
events.result: A shared workspace was set up and an AI-assisted rough model made; the URDF mesh was converted to a solid, found not to scale, rescaled, and a complete assembly with wheels was uploaded. A further hand-drawn component model was also shared.

events.title: Payload mounting reviewed: platform plate and rails instead of cam clamp
events.result: Cam clamp noted as requiring rail modification; discussion moved toward the existing payload plate and rails.

events.title: Overall module layout concept visualised; decision to build V1 without full CAD
events.result: AI-assisted layout images circulated for team review; V-shaped plate dropped for a removable plate, and the trommel angle was flagged for increase.

events.title: Drum support and drive concept sketched using four shafts with rollers
events.result: Concept used four support shafts with rollers and end constraint; friction drive from the lower shafts was suggested, with gears and chains seen as poor for sand.

events.title: Rover wiring and Pi power prepared ahead of beach test
events.result: Wiring was done in the lab, but Pi power remained unreliable with more work planned next morning, and the rover cooling fans were reported not working.

events.title: Copernicus rover driven on wet sand at West Coast beach
events.result: The rover was filmed driving on wet sand near the waterline and supervisors responded positively; no traction measurements were reported, and the team chose to proceed with building.

events.title: Supervisors invited team to apply for EUREKA challenge
events.result: The team received the invitation and noted a 2 Sept proposal deadline and a 21 Oct Innovation Day.

events.title: Drum frame CAD changed to angled connectors and 3030 rails
events.result: Rails replaced shafts in the frame design, and drum diameter of around 300 mm was treated as the practical minimum, making overall height a concern; a sliding connector was rejected in favour of printed corner brackets.

events.title: EUREKA challenge registration completed
events.result: Registration was reported complete, with the next submission date on 2 Sept.

events.title: Drum CAD set at 10-degree incline with 5 mm mesh
events.result: Height was declared final for conveyor dimensioning, with front and back rims still to be added.

events.title: Conveyor drive motor and M6 extrusion hardware purchased
events.result: A high-torque, slower motor was chosen for the conveyor, with a faster motor suggested for the drum.

events.title: Supervisor review of problem statement and prototype progress
events.result: Supervisors found the problem statement still too abstract, suggested a sustainability angle and asked for a rough first prototype as soon as possible.

events.title: Module mounting approaches compared for conveyor and drum
events.result: The conveyor used a two-point drop-in mount with a clamp, while the drum used rails and brackets on 3030; modelled mesh holes were also flagged as slowing the shared CAD.

events.title: Copernicus repair code repository shared for platform review
events.result: The repository was shared but is out of date because the latest code on the Raspberry Pi had not been pushed.

events.title: Conveyor build approach set with printed parts and 2020 extrusion
events.result: The first iteration would be mostly 3D printed, with sheet metal possible later, and 2020 extrusion was chosen to save weight over 3030.

events.title: Drum bill of materials compiled and parts purchased
events.result: The drum list covered friction-drive and gasket strips, with alternatives considered because polyurethane strip was hard to source, and the listed items were bought on 19 Aug except for T-nuts covered separately.

events.title: Payload power and motor control architecture discussed
events.result: The team favoured a separate 24 V battery instead of the current-limited board output, with a microcontroller handling motor control and sensing under serial commands from the Raspberry Pi.

events.title: Drum rim redesigned in thirds with heat-set insert holes
events.result: The rim was split into thirds because it exceeded the 260 mm print bed, and insert sizing and chamfer guidance were added before printing.

events.title: Problem statement options explored, including heat stress and work-rest limits
events.result: Options including uneven cleanliness from work-rest cycles and heat-limited working were discussed, without a final statement at this stage.

events.title: 24 V sodium-ion battery obtained and test-fitted in rover
events.result: A 504 Wh pack was obtained and placed inside the rover, with manual charging planned and runtime only estimated.

events.title: Conveyor CAD mostly complete with mesh belt selected
events.result: Most of the conveyor was modelled in the shared CAD, using an off-the-shelf baking-style mesh belt while the drum used galvanised square mesh for its first iteration.

events.title: Drum parts, motor driver and battery charging started
events.result: Parts and an XY-160D motor driver arrived, and the 24 V pack went on charge in the lab.

events.title: Conveyor skid plate and pivoting ground-following arrangement checked in CAD
events.result: The skid and conveyor were both designed to pivot freely so the skid could align itself to the ground.

events.title: Extrusion stock sourced, workshop access arranged and frame lengths cut
events.result: A cut list for 2020 and 3030 was issued, 10-degree cuts were requested and a student-team workshop became available; the exact cutting date is unclear, but cut frames appear on the rover by 28 Aug.

events.title: Drum rims and brackets printed, with one failed print restarted
events.result: Rim and bracket parts were printed, and a print fault on 26 Aug was resolved by cleaning the nozzle and restarting.

events.title: Drum motor and casters received
events.result: The motor arrived on 25 Aug and casters on 26 Aug, completing the outstanding drum parts for assembly.

events.title: Mesh drum assembled with printed rims and heat-set inserts
events.result: The mesh cylinder was assembled by the afternoon of 26 Aug, but the rubber drive strips were unsatisfactory and replacements were ordered for the following week.

events.title: Battery recovered on power supply; motor driver bench-confirmed working
events.result: The pack accepted charge again from a bench supply after the short, and the motor driver was reported working.

events.title: Conveyor shafts prepared and late-night fabrication trip to workshop
events.result: A rod was reduced for a press fit, and holes and short extrusions were listed for fabrication; workshop results are not explicitly stated.

events.title: Motor mount redesigned after motors differed in size
events.result: The first mount did not suit the two different motors, so a redo was planned and the near-term goal shifted to getting the frame out.

events.title: Caster wheel mounts batch-printed for the drum frame
events.result: Yellow caster mounts were printed in a batch and appear fitted on the frame the following day.

events.title: First integrated prototype assembled on rover with drum and conveyor frame
events.result: Photos and video show the drum frame, casters, rims and conveyor mounted on the rover with drive belt and motor under wiring; the mesh belt was not yet fitted and no powered drum or debris run is confirmed.

events.title: Supervisor review refocused problem statement on wet sand and test metrics
events.result: The focus moved to wet-sand capability, with a controlled trash-pickup comparison across sand types, an unstructured pilot and user interviews proposed as evaluation.

events.title: Drum redesign moved to bicycle rims with larger diameter
events.result: After the 28 Aug review the drum moved from printed rims to bicycle rims, starting at 16 inches and then sized around 18 inches; a first pair was reported bought by 30 Aug, with more ordered in September and integration still pending.

events.title: Frame architecture changed to posts on 4040 rails with removable subsystems
events.result: The team chose four side-attached posts rather than a full overframe that would block the conveyor, with modularity scoped to subsystem removal for wet-sand cleaning and maintenance.

events.title: Caster bearings rejected for sand; bolt-and-spacer pivot chosen to try
events.result: Ball bearings were rejected because of sand exposure, with an M8 bolt and plastic spacer design proposed in place of the earlier casters and quick-release clamp; parts were still being sourced.

events.title: Replacement 24 V battery order arrived as wrong 12 V unit
events.result: An ordered 24 V pack arrived labelled 12 V and the seller was contacted about the error.

events.title: EUREKA track application submitted
events.result: Application reported as submitted.

events.title: Bicycle rims and rim-support wheels procured for mesh drum
events.result: A top-up order brought the total to three 18-inch and three 20-inch rims, plus about 20 support wheels in several variants; rims collected by 5 Sep.

events.title: 18-inch rim measured for drum sizing
events.result: Rim profile and diameters recorded; team noted the 20-inch rim as an option because the 18-inch looked small.

events.title: U or V sand collection plate designed, with manufacturing options explored
events.result: Initial CAD made and PVC sheet with printed mounts considered; a new plate design was in progress by 13 Sep, later overtaken by the half-drum concept.

events.title: Mesh drum and 3030 support frame assembled, rigidity hand-checked
events.result: Frame arrangement and flushness were documented and the assembly was reported as rigid.

events.title: Drum and castors trial-fitted on robot; conveyor removed after bracket bending
events.result: A printed white mounting part bent because the top pin was not seated and only the quick release held it, so the conveyor was taken off; the drum was noted as able to be longer.

events.title: Sand tray fabricated with 2020 extrusion and drilled pan
events.result: Tray reported finished on 17 Sep, pending push pins, with two unused drilled holes and the motor area still to be closed off.

events.title: Team selected as EUREKA track finalist
events.result: Finalist notification received, with logo, booth and pitch video requirements following.

events.title: Shared 3D printer reliability problems during prototype printing
events.result: One shared printer was reported as unusable and repeated jamming or filament run-out pushed some prints to the hub.

events.title: First conveyor pickup run in sandpit
events.result: The setup did not work at the sandpit: the skid dug in, spokes did not grip enough, conveyor speed was too high, gears slipped, and a screw was loose.

events.title: Pushing test recorded on video
events.result: Outcome not stated in chat.

events.title: Supervisor consulted on field testing after sandpit results
events.result: Guidance was to fix sandpit issues first, then to try the beach anyway while documenting findings systematically; the team chose to arrange its own transport.

events.title: Static brush for conveyor-to-drum transfer fitted
events.result: Brush was found to be somewhat short, recorded as a small issue.

events.title: Shorter skid and revised spokes redesigned and reprinted
events.result: Work followed the sandpit findings; filament shortage forced a risky overnight print and spoke variants were limited for the next test.

events.title: Reviewer feedback widened debris scope and urged early failure testing
events.result: Feedback asked for seaweed and branches and a scoop-into-drum alternative; team noted the carton test object was out of scope and agreed to record all failures.

events.title: Overnight spoke print failed mid-job
events.result: The print detached during the job, leaving one fewer spoke iteration available for testing.

events.title: Design pivot to half-drum U plate with left-right actuation
events.result: Decision and work split were recorded after the test, including logging of results.

events.title: Scoop-style conveyor spoke designed and single part test-printed
events.result: One part appears to have been printed in-house; printing the remaining sets at the hub is not confirmed.

events.title: Conveyor width measured to size half-drum rim cut
events.result: Mesh width and overall bracket width were measured, and the rim cut angle was calculated from the 20-inch rim.

events.title: Conveyor power test recorded at 12 V 3 A
events.result: The run was recorded on video; chat indicates this setting and a suggested 24 V 2 A alternative were not adequate, without load data.

events.title: Prior-art review of beach cleaners and sand sifting machines
events.result: An existing machine range and a patent combining conveyor and tumbler separation were reviewed.

events.title: 20-inch rims cut for half-drum
events.result: Cut rims were reported ready at the makerspace by 25 Sep.

events.title: Half-drum mounts designed and printed
events.result: Mounts started at the hub on 25 Sep, delayed by hub closure, with further printing on 28 Sep; prints were being collected on 29 Sep.

events.title: Capstan rope drive for half-drum developed and string mount assembled
events.result: The mount was redone for 2 mm string with larger channel walls and was completed and shown on video on 1 Oct, with knots left removable in case of changes and rim constraint work still to follow.

events.title: Half-drum mesh and rims fabricated at makerspace
events.result: Fabrication session proceeded with mesh cutting recorded in a photo.

events.title: Half-drum v1 assembled at Studio 3
events.result: Assembly was documented with castor alignment set; rework remained for 3030 lengths, capstan mount and electronics.

events.title: EUREKA pitch deck and recording submitted; team listed on event site
events.result: Submission was acknowledged by the organiser; the deck was described internally as a draft, with its figures being targets rather than results.

events.title: Informal feedback on spoke angle and a passive folding spoke idea
events.result: Suggestion was to keep spokes flatter while scooping and lock them when lifting; the team saw variable load and debris space as open problems and built nothing from it.

events.title: Limit switch mounts printed, reworked and finished
events.result: Epoxy contamination risk led to a redo of the first switch mounting; the limit switch hardware was reported finished on 8 Oct, with wiring and software testing still to come.

events.title: Shaft rod sizes measured; steel and aluminium rods ordered and received
events.result: Bores were measured at 12.7 mm and 13.5 mm; one stainless and one aluminium 12.7 mm rod arrived on 7 Oct.

events.title: Control electronics and combined Pi and driver case built, initially untested
events.result: Electronics were declared complete on 16 Oct, including an auto-started remote access script, but team questions showed no functional test had yet been run.

events.title: Conveyor and half-drum clearance fit check, with redesign points identified
events.result: Clearance was confirmed and the setup worked for now; follow-ups were to lower the drum, move the motor aside, extend the front mesh, remake the drive and add a string tensioner.

events.title: Testing metrics document drafted and shared for team review
events.result: Draft test metrics were circulated for revision and intended to feed report sections 3 and 4.

events.title: Drive string tensioner options reviewed; inline spring selected
events.result: A proposed tensioner was rejected because the string could still loosen, and an inline spring was suggested instead; no fitting was shown in this step.

events.title: Reprinted conveyor mount fitted; clearance to front mesh checked
events.result: The conveyor cleared the mesh with room to spare, but another printed part bent enough to block its pin and was accepted for testing only.

events.title: Half-drum rim reworked and lowered using a side motor mount
events.result: The plate went back on about 2 cm lower by estimate, the side motor mount was printed on a low filament spool despite printer faults, and the angled extrusion connectors began deforming.

events.title: Conveyor mount part found broken; replacement and machining considered
events.result: An older printed mount broke, the team moved to reprinting both sides, and the supervisor suggested machining.

events.title: Haze advisory halted outdoor robot testing for following weeks
events.result: A notice asked the team not to test outdoors for the next few weeks during a severe haze period.

events.title: Extrusion slot covers and end caps sourced to keep sand out
events.result: Cover strips and caps were ordered by 20 Oct and the strips arrived on 23 Oct.

events.title: Supervisor progress meeting in the studio
events.result: A midday meeting was arranged and called minutes before its start; its content is not recorded.

events.title: Motor driver fault traced to a poor connector contact
events.result: The driver worked on Arduino but appeared to fail on the Pi until a connector contact problem was identified on 19 Oct and the driver then ran.

events.title: Powered half-drum capstan drive check before bench test
events.result: The drive ran but oscillated, and string tension was left as a follow-up.

events.title: Debris test set assembled for the first full system run
events.result: A debris list was chosen and items gathered, with three runs planned per item on dry and wet sand.

events.title: Bench test 1: first full-system debris collection runs on dry and wet sand
events.result: Mixed per-item results: small rigid items slipped through spokes, large light items were pushed ahead, sand built up at the drum and motor area, wet sand jammed the conveyor, and cracking and drive-string loosening were seen.

events.title: Raspberry Pi and motor driver stopped working; spare Pi restored boot
events.result: After limit switch soldering the Pi showed no activity light and the driver also appeared dead; a replacement Pi booted using the old SD card, and the cause was not established.

events.title: Limit switch and motor control moved to an Arduino Mega fallback
events.result: Code and pin mapping for a Mega-based limit switch and driver setup were prepared as a faster route than repairing the Pi hat.

events.title: EUREKA dry run and robot booth setup at Innovation Day venue
events.result: The pitch was rehearsed, the robot was moved to the EA venue without the sandpit for lack of space, and a senior professor briefed the team on a one-minute walkabout pitch.

events.title: Angled frame brackets redesigned, reprinted and replaced on rim frame
events.result: Enlarged-hole mounts were fitted and considered sturdier, but the conveyor then struck the front mesh and the rim looked misaligned; machining was discussed but nothing was sent as of 21 Oct.

events.title: EUREKA final pitch delivered at CDE Innovation Day
events.result: The team pitched as a finalist from a larger field after a slot change, with no award indicated; the hoped-for prior beach video of pickup is not confirmed.

events.title: Rover driving test with payload, EA to E2A, then sandpit locomotion
events.result: Drive and limited turning on sand were demonstrated, but higher gear or fast turns caused motor overcurrent stalls and, with the conveyor attached, serial control faults.

events.title: Printed front hood prototype tried for large light items
events.result: The hood was found to interfere with the mechanism and the team moved to another concept.

events.title: Belt drive trial on half-drum rim
events.result: The belt slipped heavily because the small teeth and printed mount gave too little grip, and thicker belts or a return to capstan were raised.

events.title: Plastic mesh added to spokes for small item capture
events.result: Plastic mesh covering about half the spoke was fitted, with a metal version to follow; extending mesh to all spokes stayed on the later to-do list.

events.title: Mentor review of final presentation framing
events.result: Advice was to add slides on the general robotics problem solved rather than focus only on deployment.

events.title: Ratcheted three-flap front sweeper trial for large light items
events.result: Items rotated the sweeper backwards, so stiffer flap materials were added to the to-do list.

events.title: Friction drive and spring-constrained rim development after belt failure
events.result: Springs were obtained and a printed shaft-mounted friction wheel was specified as a must-work item, but no successful run is shown by 29 Oct.

events.title: Integration session in place of planned bench test 2
events.result: The team met after lunch and a drum fix list followed, including clumping wet sand and slipping drive, but no bench test 2 run or results are recorded.
